gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Starborn drifts, with wide gaps and a dark stripe of lowercase. Noto Sans Marchen keeps its small letters nearly capital-sized, with curves ending in clear daylight, so the drift above has something sturdy to land on.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Starborn floats its dreamy heading over wide gaps and a dark stripe of lowercase. Noto Sans Nag Mundari then reads steadily, its lowercase rivaling the capitals and its curves looking half unwrapped.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Spacious, dreamy drift up top: that is Starborn. Noto Sans Nushu sets a towering x-height plus far-held terminals against it, and that gap in temperament is the whole appeal.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Starborn drifts, wide-spaced and dreamy, with a dark lowercase stripe. Noto Sans Ogham continues with tall, bold-looking lowercase and wide gaps in the e, so extended reading feels open and sturdy.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-hun: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads friendly and current, with large open counters in tall a, e and s that stay open when tiny. Starborn can stay large, its dark lowercase stripe doing the work.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-ita: Dreamy sprawl, wide gaps, a dark lowercase stripe: that is Starborn over a sans-serif. And Noto Sans Old Italic, with curve endings kept apart, can happily stay small in size.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-old-sog: Dreamy drift, all gaps and dark stripe: Starborn. Noto Sans Old Sogdian, a sans-serif, counters with a tall x-height nearly reaching cap height, wide-mouthed letters staying crisp when shrunk.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Noto Sans Oriya reads approachable and current. Starborn is best at dreamy drift and a dark lowercase stripe, while the sans body is best at generous curves and small letters nearly capital-tall.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-samarit: Noto Sans Samaritan reads approachable and sturdy, its curves holding plenty of daylight inside a hefty lowercase. Made small, Starborn would lose much of its dreamy gaps and dark stripe.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Wide gaps between letters and a thick, dark lowercase stripe make Starborn feel dreamy and ethereal. Noto Sans Sharada anchors it with clean, open c forms and bulky proportions.
